steps.message:
# Ship is damaged when performing the action shown in the recording

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a ship performing an action at a station. The action does not
go the way it is set up to go, and the ship does not come out of it unharmed.
The collision outlines of the ship and the pad already overlap while the ship sits still, although the video shows it resting clear of the pad. The ship in the video is not the one the game starts you with; work out which ship it is first. A ship that really lands on a pad must still be caught by it, and the ship must keep its overall proportions.

### Expected
Performing the action shown in the recording must not damage the ship at all, at the spot shown in
the video or at any other equivalent spot of the same station. The hull-integrity readout stays at
100% for the whole action.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect the video frame by frame with `ffmpeg` (installed in the image), e.g. extracting
still frames at specific timestamps to look closely at the HUD and the ship.

Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it does
not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from collections import Counter
NS='{http://www.collada.org/2005/11/COLLADASchema}'
r=ET.parse('new_ground_landing.dae').getroot()
geoms={}
for g in r.iter(f'{NS}geometry'):
    m=g.find(f'{NS}mesh')
    vid=m.find(f'{NS}vertices/{NS}input[@semantic="POSITION"]').get('source')[1:]
    src=[s for s in m.findall(f'{NS}source') if s.get('id')==vid][0]

    geoms[g.get('id')]=[v[i:i+3] for i in range(0,len(v),3)]
for n in r.iter(f'{NS}node'):

    mx=n.find(f'{NS}matrix').text
    ig=n.find(f'{NS}instance_geometry')
    print(nm, mx)
    if ig is not None:
        P=geoms[ig.get('url')[1:]]
        print('   nverts',len(P),'z values',sorted(Counter(round(p[2],3) for p in P).items()), 'x',min(p[0] for p in P),max(p[0] for p in P))
EOF

steps.message:
I've fixed two data errors that would damage a ship docking at a ground station, but I couldn't confirm it in the game. `/app/.harbor_assets/` was empty, so I never saw the recording. I worked from the written description plus a scripted comparison of every ship and station model. I also didn't build or run the game, so the claim that hull integrity now stays at 100% is untested.

**Which ship:** probably the **Skipjack**. The starting ships are the Coronatrix, Pumpkinseed and Xylophis. Of all ships, only the Skipjack had a landing-height error. Without the video I can't confirm it's the one in the recording.

**1. Skipjack low-detail model** (`data/models/ships/skipjack/skipjack_low.dae`)
- Each ship model has a `tag_landing` marker that sets how high the ship sits on a pad. The game loads the low-detail version first and keeps the first marker it finds, so this file's marker is the one used.
- That marker was at −3.861, while the high and medium versions and the bottom of the collision hull are all at −4.311. A docked Skipjack therefore sat 0.45 m inside the pad.
- I set it to −4.310857. The marker is the only change, so the ship keeps its size and proportions.

**2. `new_ground` station pads** (`data/models/stations/new_ground/new_ground_landing.dae`)
- The visible pad surface and the landing markers are at height 72.582, but every pad's collision box was higher. Pads 2–6 were 0.255 m too high, and pad 1 (the first one handed out) was 0.725 m too high.
- So a ship that looked like it was resting on the pad was actually inside the pad's collision box. That matches "rests clear of the pad but the outlines overlap".
- I moved all six collision boxes so their tops sit exactly at 72.582. The boxes are still there, so a ship that lands is still caught by the pad. The docking autopilot also aims 0.1 m below the pad surface, so it will still make contact.

After the fix, the top of every pad's collision box on that station is level with its landing marker. A docked Skipjack's collision hull now just touches the pad surface rather than sitting inside it. There are no compiled model caches that could override these files.

I left the other ground station alone. Its small pads 09 and 13 are 0.094 m above their markers, but that looks like how they were originally made, and the Skipjack is too big to use them. Nothing is committed.
